title: Zoom in: the publish path never loses a post event and splits big jobs
caption: An outbox makes 'post saved' and 'event published' one decision; a planner cuts each fan-out into small batches that any worker can retry.

steps.text: The post API inserts the post and an outbox row in the same database transaction: either both exist or neither does.
A relay tails the outbox and publishes each row to the event log, marking it sent only after the log acknowledges.
The planner reads the follower count and cuts the job into batches of 1 000 follower ids (a cursor range, not the ids themselves).
Any free worker takes a batch, reads that page of the follow graph and writes the post id into those timelines in one pipelined call.
A batch is acknowledged only after its writes land, so a crash means that one batch is retried, not the whole post.

scenarios.name: Big author, many batches
scenarios.summary: A post from an account just under the celebrity threshold becomes 400 batches that the pool drains in parallel.

steps.text: 400 k followers become 400 batch jobs in a few milliseconds.
The pool scales out on queue depth; 50 workers drain it in seconds instead of one worker for minutes.
Small authors' batches sit in the same queue, so one big post doesn't delay everyone else's by more than a few seconds.

scenarios.name: Relay crash
scenarios.summary: Without the outbox, a crash between 'save' and 'publish' silently loses the fan-out. With it, the post is only delayed.

steps.text: The post and its outbox row are committed.
A new relay starts, finds the unsent row and publishes it. If the old one had already published, the event appears twice.
The planner dedupes by post id, so followers get the post once, a few seconds late.

scenarios.name: Timeline shard slow
scenarios.summary: One timeline shard degrades: retries with backoff, and a dead-letter queue so poisoned batches don't block the pool.

steps.text: Writes to one timeline shard start timing out.
Workers retry those batches with exponential backoff; batches for healthy shards keep flowing.
After 5 failed attempts a batch goes to the dead-letter queue and an alert fires; it is replayed once the shard recovers.
